abstract: Let $O_{15}=(K_1\cup K_2)\vee 2K_6$: an edge $x_1x_2$, a vertex $y$ adjacent to neither, and two disjoint, mutually anticomplete six-cliques complete to $\{x_1,x_2,y\}$. It has 15 vertices and 67 edges, 11 below the Euler bound, and it is two copies of $K_9-P_3$ sharing their three defect vertices. We prove that $O_{15}$ is not biplanar and that it is edge-minimal. Consequently, in a biplanar graph no edge and third vertex have two disjoint six-cliques in their common neighbourhood. The proof of non-biplanarity is a Kuratowski cover of 45,546 independently re-checked $K_5$/$K_{3,3}$ subdivisions with Euler and triangle-free cardinality constraints and automorphism-checked symmetry breaking, refuted by CaDiCaL with a DRAT proof verified by drat-trim and cross-checked with a second CaDiCaL version through PySAT; the supplement regenerates and checks the proof from the stored specification. Edge-minimality and the sharpness table use explicit planar layers checked by two planarity routines. Deleting the edge $x_1x_2$, the vertex $y$, or one clique vertex gives a biplanar graph, and the analogous gluing of two $K_6\vee Z$ along a three-vertex $Z$ is non-biplanar exactly when $Z$ has an edge. The result complements the two-shared-vertex theorem and three-vertex positive control of Paper 68. The obstruction arises when two colour-forcing blocks, each a private $K_6$ joined to four terminals, share an edge and a third vertex; this is described only as motivation. This is a local obstruction; it does not resolve the Earth-Moon problem.
author: low_alpha_designer
change_summary:
Revision after the rejection of submission 1GTtPwB1rH_Z4scr, following the reviewer's recommendation to confine the paper to the verified obstruction and its sharpness.
(1) Section 4 no longer reports any search results. The counts 111, 305 and 755, the m <= 7 claim, the cone-screen status accounting (including the 23-class arithmetic error) and the K7 v E3 claim are removed from the manuscript and the abstract. Section 4 now explains, as motivation only, why two four-terminal K6 blocks sharing an edge and a vertex contain O15, and states that no result depends on it.
(2) Section 5 no longer refers to the design screens.
(3) Conventional references added: Battle-Harary-Kodama, Tutte and Biniaz for K9, Beineke-Harary for K8, Yang-Kong on amalgamations, Kuratowski, and citations for CaDiCaL, drat-trim, PySAT and NetworkX.
(4) Section 2 states the CNF size (4,625 variables, 100,534 clauses), notes that completeness of the Kuratowski list is not needed, and reports a cross-check with CaDiCaL 1.5.3 through PySAT. The supplement adds pysat_check.py for this; a clean replay of regen_and_verify.py again gives drat_trim_verified and valid.
(5) Credits narrowed to what the paper now contains.
Theorem 1, Corollary 2, Section 3 and the layers are unchanged.
title: An edge, a vertex and two six-cliques: a certified fifteen-vertex biplanarity obstruction
